title: Integrated genomic and transcriptomic profiling identifies PFKM as a candidate biomarker of nodal metastasis in oral squamous cell carcinoma
html:
Highlights

  • •

    PFKM (phosphofructokinase, muscle type) marks pN stage across molecular levels.

  • •

    WNT2 and PTH1R are enriched in advanced nodal-stage oral squamous cell carcinoma.

  • •

    Whole-exome sequencing validates metastasis candidate genes in tumor specimens.

  • •

    Epithelial–mesenchymal transition, myogenesis, and metabolism are enriched.

Objectives

Nodal metastasis is a key prognostic determinant in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), yet its underlying molecular basis remains poorly defined. This study aimed to identify prognostic genes and pathways associated with nodal metastasis in OSCC using integrated genomic, transcriptomic, and experimental approaches.

Design

Genomic and transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas and Gene Expression Omnibus were analyzed to compare pN2 and pN0 OSCC tumors and identify differentially mutated and expressed genes. Pathway enrichment analyses were conducted using gene set enrichment, Gene Ontology, and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes analyses. Candidate genes were validated by WES in 28 institutional OSCC specimens, and their expression was assessed by RT-qPCR in metastatic OSCC cell lines.

Results

Nine metastasis-associated prognostic genes—WNT2, PTH1R, PFKM, CCDC59, ACTN2, ARL4C, KCTD9, DLGAP3, and PITPNM3—were identified across pN0 and pN2 stages. Among these, PFKM showed the most consistent multi-level association, characterized by increased DNA mutation frequency, elevated RNA expression in pN2 tumors, unfavorable survival outcomes, and upregulation in highly metastatic OSCC cell lines. WNT2 and PTH1R similarly demonstrated increased mutation burden and transcript expression in pN2 samples, whereas KCTD9 exhibited features consistent with negative regulation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Pathway analyses revealed enrichment of epithelial–mesenchymal transition, actin cytoskeletal remodeling, myogenesis, and metabolic programs in pN2 tumors, while immune- and inflammation-related processes predominated in pN0 tumors.

Conclusions

This integrated analysis identifies PFKM as a stable biomarker candidate associated with nodal metastasis in OSCC and highlights the coordinated involvement of metabolic and Wnt/β-catenin–related pathways in metastatic progression.
